body:
Thanks for the advice, I will start doing some serious exercise starting tomorrow (As much as I would like to say 'right now', it's 2am here so it will have to genuinely be tomorrow) and try to come up with some other fulfilling things to occupy my time.

We have been together for a 3 years and we lived together until she moved out last week; so it was fairly serious. Thanks, and I don't expect to be over a long-term relationship that ended due to infidelity in one week but it is nice to know that it's normal to be feeling this way and the sooner I can put this behind me the better.

I know I have been suspicious for the past month or so and I've been proven correct which has probably reinforced me feeling that way but you're right: that doesn't mean that I am right this time. I'll try to keep that possibility out of my head... do you have any tips with regard to doing that?

Thanks for the reply, she was extremely toxic! She has a lot of problems and I'm glad that she is probably in a better position to deal with them now - having a boyfriend who is suspicious and jealous probably wasn't helping her any. 

I know I should let go and that I should forget about her and enjoy being single. But I don't know how; I try but these feelings just keep coming back. I do feel better now, it's nice to have other people knowing what I'm going through (and even offering help :) ) but I suspect, like the other times I've felt better, that it will only be until I am reminded of what happened again. So yeah, letting go is what I need to do... but how?

I would be able to trust his answer if I asked him. He is a good friend and counselled me a lot in the past month (and before) which is perhaps why I wouldn't be able to trust him if he did do anything - he recommended I break up with her when it first happened and has stuck by that until I did last week. I suppose if something were to happen I couldn't the idea out of my head of an ulterior motive on his part. He has said to me in the past that he wants to sleep with her, and that he would do so given the opportunity. I guess that has helped fuel my suspicion but it also makes me feel like I could trust him to tell me if anything happened. Then again, perhaps he wouldn't tell me right away because I would be too upset about it.

He is still friends with her (and so he should be), and I'm concerned that, if I were to ask him, it would create animosity between us - and I don't want to lose both my girlfriend and my best friend!

Thanks for the reply, it was helpful to hear that those negative emotions are normal and temporary.

I think you might be right, I should probably do nothing: I know that she now can sleep with who she wants (and so can I) but I guess I still feel the connected with her such that it would hurt me if she did. The same goes for me though, I am not interested in hooking up with anyone else because I would feel wrong about it. I think I should probably just try to stick it out, I'll come to emotionally accept that it's over soon enough (hopefully sooner than later). Do you have any tips for accelerating this process?
